evidence: Steps are: open PowerToys Run, then press Win+Comma.
The expected comparison is Command Palette closing, while Run leaves a ghost window.
PowerLauncher MainWindow handles Deactivated and delegates to MainViewModel.Hide when HideWhenDeactivated is enabled.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run leaves a visible ghost surface after Win+Comma while open; the report has concise steps and a recording.
known_information: The report was captured on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
Win+D does not produce the same behavior according to the reporter.
A video attachment demonstrates the ghost surface.
inferences: The Win+Comma desktop-peek transition may exercise a deactivation or composition sequence different from Win+D.
The ghost may be a visibility/animation/compositor state rather than a normal active Run window.
issue_context.analysis: The behavior is specific enough to reproduce and compare against another shell shortcut. Fast triage should preserve uncertainty about the exact UI mechanism while routing investigation to the existing deactivation and hide seams.
initial_investigation: MainWindow.xaml.cs hides through the view model when HideWhenDeactivated is configured.
No duplicate, assignee, or linked fix appears in the issue timeline.
